articleTitle: A Complementary Global and Local Knowledge Network for Ultrasound Denoising with Fine-grained Refinement
abstract: Ultrasound imaging serves as an effective and noninvasive diagnostic tool commonly employed in clinical examinations. However, the presence of speckle noise invariably degrades image quality, impeding the performance of subsequent tasks, such as classification and segmentation. Existing methods for speckle noise reduction frequently induce excessive image smoothing or fail to preserve detailed information adequately. In this paper, we propose a complementary global and local knowledge network for ultrasound denoising with fine-grained refinement. Initially, the proposed architecture employs the L-CSwinTransformer as encoder to capture global information, incorporating CNN as decoder to fuse local features. We expand the resolution of the feature at different stages to extract more global information compared to the original CSwinTransformer. Subsequently, we integrate Fine-grained Refinement Block (FRB) within the skip-connection stage to further augment features. We validate our model on two public datasets, HC18 and BUSI. Experimental results demonstrate that our model can achieve competitive performance in both quantitative metrics and visual performance.

articleTitle: Prescribed-time Non-overshooting Tracking Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: This study proposes the prescribed-time non-overshooting tracking scheme for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Considering the nonlinear nature of the motor’s torque and the interaction between rotational speed and current, the establishment of the prescribed-time non-overshooting tracking control strategy for PMSM involves numerous challenges. By utilizing barrier functions associated with the desired signal and restrained boundaries and incorporating a subtle time-varying function related with the instant prescribed time, we devise new continuous state-feedback tracking control strategy including prescribed-time non-overshooting direct axis current tracking scheme and prescribed-time non-overshooting position tracking controller. Compared with the current results of PMSM, the new tracking scheme assures that the tracking error converges to the orgin within a instant of the prescribed time and achieving the guaranteed performance which is featured by non-overshooting tracking error and inviolate output asymmetric time-varying constraints. At last, simulations results demonstrate the practicality of the presented scheme.

articleTitle: A Torque Ripple Suppression Method of Sensorless Control for Five-phase PMSM Based on High-frequency Signal Injection
abstract: To effectively tackle the issue of high-frequency torque ripple in five-phase motors, this paper presents a novel method for suppressing high-frequency torque ripple through sensorless control in five-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors. This innovative approach is specifically designed to address the problem of high-frequency torque ripple and ensure its suppression in the motor. Compared with traditional methods, this strategy chooses to inject two high-frequency voltage signals with the same frequency but different amplitudes simultaneously on the d-axis and q-axis. Through this scheme, the optimal ratio of these two voltage amplitudes is determined to ensure that the electromagnetic torque remains stable during the signal injection process. Through this method, a constant d-axis and q-axis currents can be achieved, thereby minimizing high-frequency torque fluctuations. Through simulation verification, this strategy has shown significant effectiveness in solving the problem of high-frequency torque fluctuations in five phase motors. This optimized high-frequency signal injection method provides a new approach for optimizing the transmission performance of sensorless five phase motor, significantly reducing the vibration and noise generated by the driving system and improving overall operating efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel Prescribed Finite-Time Attitude Tracking Control of Quadrotor UAVs
abstract: This paper presents a novel attitude tracking control strategy for quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) based on the backstepping technique, which achieves prescribed finitetime stability. The main contribution lies in the development of a controller that integrates Lyapunov stability theory, prescribed finite-time control and backstepping methodologies to ensure rapid and precise convergence of attitude errors to zero within a predefined time. Unlike traditional finite-time and fixed-time control approaches, the proposed controller exhibits a significant advantage by possessing a convergence time independent of initial conditions and design parameters, which greatly improves the control accuracy. The efficacy of the proposed control scheme is rigorously proven through mathematical analysis, demonstrating the prescribed finite-time stability of the quadrotor system. Simulation results further validate the superior performance of the controller, highlighting its potential to enhance the operational efficiency and safety of quadrotor UAVs.

articleTitle: Distributed fault estimation intermediate observer design for a class of stochastic multi-agent systems
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of robust distributed fault estimation in stochastic multi-agent systems (MASs), employing an innovative approach based on intermediate observers. We assume a directed communication topology for the MASs under consideration. Our method presents a new distributed intermediate estimator, engineered to accurately determine the systems internal state in real-time, even amidst faults and random disturbances. By developing a precise error system model, we facilitate a thorough analysis of the discrepancies between actual and estimated states, thus guaranteeing the system’s eventual bounded stability. The efficacy of our methodology is demonstrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Intelligent Prototype Generation Method On Machine Fault Diagnosis Through Compressing Large Dataset
abstract: In modern industries, machine condition monitoring data have been available for improved maintenance. While big data generally benefits intelligent fault diagnosis performance, the significantly increased data amount inevitably poses high requirements for storage and computation. As a consequence, it is very difficult for the fault diagnosis model to be updated and applied efficiently. In order to address this issue, an intelligent prototype generation method is proposed in this paper. First, a deep convolutional neural network is used as the main framework, which is pre-trained to generate data prototype from large amounts of raw data. Next, the loss of raw data and prototypes is calculated in high-level spatial representations. The model weights are fixed and the prototypes are updated correspondingly. Furthermore, considering the interference of noise and further expanding the variety of the raw dataset, an in-process data augmentation method is proposed, which improves the robustness of prototypes. The performance of the proposed method is validated on a practical dataset collected from a gear failure simulation system. The results show that the proposed method has the ability to compress a large dataset into a lightweight one with prototypes, while achieving similar diagnosis accuracy. In this way, the data storage and computation requirements can be largely relaxed for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of Tuning Platform for Micro-turbojet Aircraft
abstract: Micro-turbojet is widely used in civil aviation due to high thrust-to-weight ratio, superior combustion efficiency and low fuel consumption. In order to exert the operation effect of micro-turbojet aircraft, it is very important to adjust the parameters of PID controller. The efficiency and accuracy of parameter tuning tests are determined by the platform used. However, existing platforms are limited to single tests, making the process complex and reliant on the experience of testing personnel. In order to optimize the tuning test of micro-turbojet aircraft, this study designed a new aircraft tuning platform based on BP neural network and fuzzy algorithm. The platform focuses on controlling the steering gear and electric cylinder. It adjusts the multidimensional parameters of the aircraft and determines the thrust of each turbojet engine, serving as the basis for evaluating optimization effects. This ensures improved adaptability and robustness of the aircraft. The feasibility of the parameter adjustment platform is verified by simulation. The tracking error peak value is ±0.088, which realizes the goal of multiple parameter adjustment in a single test. The results of this study offer robust support for advancing micro-turbojet technology. They also establish a solid foundation for extending its application into areas such as unmanned aerial vehicles and small-scale commercial aircraft.

articleTitle: Fault Classification Method based on Self-paced Neighborhood Preserving Embedding
abstract: In view of the large amount of faulty data in industrial systems, strong correlation between data, large redundancy, and high dimensionality, traditional classification methods can easily lead to the phenomenon of "dimensionality disaster". On the basis of the Neighborhood Preserving Embedding algorithm (NPE), a fault classification algorithm based on Self-paced NPE is proposed. First, the neighbor point set and adjacency matrix of the fault sample points are obtained through the NPE algorithm. Secondly, the function of solving the projection matrix in the NPE algorithm is used as the loss function in the Self-paced Learning model to construct the objective function of the Self-paced Neighborhood Preserving Embedding (Self-paced NPE) algorithm. By designing the loss function in the Self-paced Learning model, gradually select from easy to difficult samples with smaller loss are selected, samples with larger loss are discarded, and relatively simple samples are used for training. Finally, the objective function of the Self-paced NPE algorithm is solved and the proposed algorithm is tested with TE process data . The experimental results show that, compared with the NPE algorithm, the Self-paced NPE algorithm can extract features of high-dimensional fault data more effectively, achieve dimension reduction, and improve the accuracy of fault classification.

articleTitle: Hazardous Gas Monitoring System for Power Cable Tunnel Based on PID and MLPNN
abstract: With the increasing demand for safety assurance in underground power cable tunnels, an online Photoionization Detector (PID) gas monitoring and fault warning system for cables was designed. A gas data acquisition hardware platform for cable tunnels was built using PID modules, ZigBee communication networks, and GD32 microchip. The data collected by the platform were transmitted to a data server using a 5G communication module. A monitoring center was developed to monitor Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) in real time. The system processed signal noise caused by complex power tunnel environments using a signal noise, eliminating noise interference and sensor voltage mutations. The Multi-layer Perception Neural Network (MLPNN) was built to solve the cross-sensitivity problem commonly found in gas sensors and improve data accuracy. An improved particle swarm optimization algorithm was introduced to accelerate network convergence and achieve early warning of VOC concentration anomalies in power tunnels.

articleTitle: A Novel Fixed-time-based Unmanned Surface Vehicle Autonomous Berthing Sliding Mode Control
abstract: The development of autonomous berthing system is the key to realize vehicle autonomous navigation system. Accurate trajectory tracking is crucial for autonomous berthing of unmanned surface vehicles(USVs). In this paper, a novel fixed-time autonomous berthing sliding mode control scheme is proposed, which introduces the fixed-time into the design of sliding mode surface. Compared with the traditional method, this method not only keeps the advantage of avoiding singularity, but also has faster convergence performance, and the convergence time is bounded by a constant, independent of the initial state. In addition, the discontinuous terms of the existing control algorithm are replaced with non-smooth terms to completely eliminate chattering. Finally, the simulation and comparison experiments show that the proposed control scheme is better than the typical control scheme.

articleTitle: Efficient Shunted Transformer via DPnP module
abstract: Recently, Vision Transformers show superiority and promise on various vision tasks owing to the unique long-range modeling capability of the self-attention mechanism. Although effective, it suffers from redundant attention on non-important regions like background, which inevitably increase the computational overhead. In this paper, we design a deformable poll and pool (DPnP) module to compress the key, value feature maps to retain the important features at fine granularity and compress the rest features at coarse granularity. Applying the DPnP module to the shunted self-attention significantly reduces attention redundancy, allowing for more computational space allocated to key foreground object regions, achieving more efficient shunted self-attention. The experiments demonstrate its effectiveness on the Intel-Image-Classification dataset, obtaining better top-1 accuracy, achieving 0.23% higher with 10.6% reduction of parameters.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Localization Algorithm Based on Cubature Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive event-triggered localization algorithm based on cubature Kalman filter (AETCKF), which addresses the challenge of moving targets based on received signal strength (RSS). Firstly, in order to improve communication and energy efficiency, an adaptive event triggering mechanism based on the distribution of anchors in the environment is developed, which guarantees that the number of triggered anchors is near the anticipated number, regardless of how anchors are distributed around the mobile node. Secondly, the fusion estimation of the distances is carried out using the cubature Kalman filter, where the distances between the service anchors and the mobile node is computed using the loss relationship between the energy and the path. Finally, a precise state estimate of the mobile node can be acquired for the fusion estimation step. Numerical simulation results show that the proposed method offers advantages in reducing energy consumption, communication burdens, and computational complexity while ensuring localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Soft Sensor Modeling Method for Grinding Particle Size Using IRVFLN with Compact Constraints
abstract: The quality of grinding particle size is directly related to the concentrate grade and recovery rate in flotation. Through the analysis of the production status and basic production data of the actual grinding process, it is evident that there are issues such as high online detection costs, long lag times, and implementation difficulties associated with grinding particle size. Therefore, this article establishes an incremental random weights neural network with compact constraints (IRCC) grinding particle size prediction model. This model utilizes compact constraints to select high-quality hidden parameters, thereby establishing a highly generalized model. Furthermore, this article proves the universal approximation property of the proposed IRCC. Experimental results on actual grinding data demonstrate that IRCC exhibits excellent performance in predicting grinding particle size.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle Detection in Right Turn Blind Zone of Autonomous-rail Rapid Transit Based on Fisheye Image
abstract: The Autonomous-rail Rapid Transit (ART) significantly enhances residents’ travel and promotes the development of smart cities. However, given its unique left-side driving mode, there exists a potential safety hazard when making right turns. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an intelligent method using fisheye images for blind zone detection during ART’s right turns. Firstly, fisheye cameras are used to capture fisheye images, and the dual longitude method is employed for distortion correction. Secondly, a vehicle detection method based on Single Shot Multibox Detector (SSD) is proposed, which combines Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism, Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and Dilation Block (DB), called SFD-SSD. Ablation experiments show a 5.31% mean average precision (mAP) increase on BDD100k and 7.68% on VOC datasets compared to baselines. Finally, the proposed cross-longitude distance measurement method demonstrates an average detection error of 3% for forward distance and 9.8% for lateral distance, providing convenience for ART’s assisted driving.

articleTitle: Control Framework for Stability and Comfort in Distributed Drive Electric Vehicles
abstract: In this study, we propose a novel control framework aimed at improving the stability and comfort of distributed drive electric vehicles (DDEVs). Leveraging the classical two degrees of freedom (2DOF) vehicle model, we compute the desired yaw rate and lateral deviation angle, which serve as reference signals for the model predictive control (MPC) controller. To objectively quantify and describe ride comfort, we establish a comfort domain boundary integrated into the MPC controller. Subsequently, we calculate total additional yaw moments using constrained MPC and allocate torque based on a tire load optimization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our control framework through a co-simulation experiment involving CarSim and Matlab/Simulink. Our results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances both vehicle stability and comfort.

articleTitle: A Multi-scale Feature Hierarchical Aggregation Network for Neurosurgical scene Segmentation
abstract: Neurosurgical scene segmentation can provide surgeons with the real-time location and perimeter details of important tissues and instruments. The anatomical structure representation of surgical instruments and tissues can contribute to evaluating surgical skills, tracking surgical instruments and carrying out intraoperative navigation. However, some inherent limitations including the scale variability, local similarity and interclass similarity of instruments and tissues, bring bottlenecks for accurate segmentation. To address these challenges, we propose a Multi-Scale Feature Hierarchical Aggregation Network (MFHA-Net). Specially, attention-based multi-scale feature hierarchical fusion module (AMFHF), multi-layer feature aggregation and high-level semantic guidance module (MFAASG) are designed to deal with the scale change and similarity of surgical instruments and tissues. We use pre-trained Resnet50 as the feature extraction backbone to obtain channel and spatial semantic features, while The AMFHF module is employed to enhance the features of different scales using the attention mechanism, enabling adaptation to scale changes across various targets. In addition, AMFHF module combines multi-scale features with different receptive fields, using high-layer semantic information to guide low-layer feature transmission, which can improve the model's feature discriminative ability. A neurosurgical dataset named Neuro including a variety of neurosurgical surgical instruments and brain anatomy is constructed. The proposed network in this paper achieves the best performance on the Neuro dataset, attaining the highest accuracy metrics of 68.72% MIoU, 80.09% Dice, 81.92% aAcc, and 88.32% mAcc.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Trajectory Tracking Control of Ship Autopilot System With Quantitative Performance Specifications
abstract: This paper is concerned with the trajectory tracking control problem with quantitative performance guarantees for a kind of ship autopilot system subject to model uncertainties. A novel prescribed performance control strategy is presented to cope with this problem. In the control design, a pair of novel performance functions are constructed, which not only offers a quantitative means to regulate the overshoot, peak value, settling time, and tracking accuracy but also guarantees that the initial condition holds naturally. In particular, the zero-overshoot attribute of the output tracking error is ensured when its initial value is nonzero. Furthermore, the presented approach is free of parameter identification, function approximation, or derivative calculation, thus rendering the controller structurally simple and computationally efficient. Finally, the above theoretical findings are clarified and verified via a simulation experiment.

articleTitle: A Semi-Nested Point Cloud Autoencoder for Solder Joint Inspection
abstract: As a One-class learning method, autoencoder has excellent performance in a variety of anomaly detection tasks, including one-dimensional sequences and two-dimensional image data. However, there are few studies on one-class classification methods for 3D data. In particular, in actual working conditions, due to improper assembly and other reasons, the target point cloud pose is often random within a certain range, it is difficult for the autoencoder to fit the generated point cloud to all poses of the target sample, which leads to performance degradation and thus brings additional challenges. To improve this disadvantageous situation, a uniquely designed Semi-Nested Point Cloud Autoencoder (SN-PAE) is proposed. SN-PAE first uses a rotation-invariant point cloud autoencoder to learn rotationinvariant descriptive latent variables, and then measures the latent variables by a semi-nested Latent Autoencoding Module (LAM). This avoids point cloud measurement and makes SN-PAE a more robust measurement method. In addition, we implement a set of experiments using solder joints as an example, and the results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Cascaded Network for Airway Tree Segmentation Incorporating Multiple Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Airway tree segmentation is crucial for diagnosing and treating lung diseases. A three-dimensional representation of the patient's airway tree serves as the foundation for bronchoscopic navigation, instrumental for preoperative planning and intraoperative visualization during intervention procedures. However, certain inherent characteristics such as complex structure, scale variation, and class imbalance often result in inadequate segmentation. To mitigate these limitations, we propose a cascaded airway tree segmentation network named Spatial-Channel-Deformable Cascade Network (SCD-CascadeNet). It consists of two main stages: coarse segmentation and fine segmentation. The coarse segmentation network swiftly localizes the major airways, while the fine segmentation network offers more precise segmentation of the peripheral minor airways. Specifically, the Spatial-Channel-Deformable Attention module (SCDA) is designed to capture crucial spatial regions and significant channel features within the skip connection of the fine segmentation network, thereby enhancing the network's ability to recognize tubular structures and peripheral airways. We evaluate our method using the challenging dataset named Airway Tree Modeling (ATM). Both qualitative and quantitative experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance and holds promise for further clinical applications.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Classification Method Based on CNN for Interventional EEG Data
abstract: Interventional brain-computer interfaces (BCI) have been developed for many years and are capable of collecting electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, research on interventional EEG signals is just beginning. In this paper. We present a new deep learning network for intentional classification of interventional EEG in a monkey. Electrodes are placed on the inner walls of the vessels in the superior sagittal sinus to collect signals in four states. Then, we construct a Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) model to extract features and classify the states. In the experiments, we recognize the interventional EEG signals of the monkey in the four states, and the average recognition accuracy of its EEG signals in each state is more than 90% for the whole dataset, and 70% for the validation set. The experimental results show that the method in this paper can effectively recognize and classify interventional EEG signals in different states. Our work advances the application of interventional BCIs and paves the way for the future development of more versatile and responsive interventional EEG interfaces.

articleTitle: Integrating Criss-Cross Attention Mechanism for Origin Traceability of Peanuts Using Electronic Nose Technology
abstract: Significant variations in quality are observed among peanuts sourced from different regions. This study proposes a rapid, non-destructive method for assessing peanut quality. Gas information from peanuts sourced from seven different regions is collected using an electronic nose (e-nose) system. A method combining Criss-Cross Attention (CCA) and convolutional computation is designed to extract features of gas information in terms of time series and cross-sensitivity. Lastly, global features are constructed through Recurrent Criss-Cross Attention (RCCA) to address the limitation of convolution in representing global information. The RCCA-Net achieves an accuracy of 97.85%, precision of 97.92%, and recall of 97.78%. In summary, RCCA-Net offers a practical technical solution for quality control in the food industry by successfully identifying quality variations between peanuts sourced from various geographical areas.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 SAR Image Aircraft Object Detection Method
abstract: Due to the poor model detection accuracy, easy overfitting and weak generalization in aircraft target detection under complex background in SAR images, this thesis introduces an enhanced SAR aircraft object detection algorithm, YOLOv8-GD, which is based on the YOLOv8 framework. The Gather-and-Distribute (GD) machine were used to enhance the capability of multi-scale feature fusion and improve the correct prediction rate. The GSConv is employed in the backbone network, and Wise-IoU (WIoU) loss function are used to raise the detection accuracy of the target and refine the model’s generalizability. Experiments were carried out on the SAR-Aircraft-1.0 dataset. In comparison to the current mainstream methods, the accuracy of detecting Aircraft targets in SAR images was effectively improved, which reflected the robustness and application potential of YOLOv8-GD method in aircraft target detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach: Enhancing Data Extraction from Student Handwritten Notes Using Multi-Task U-net and GPT-4
abstract: Handwritten notes by students are a critical data source reflecting their learning status. Traditionally, educators have had to review these notes individually to gauge students' comprehension and mastery of course material. However, this method is time-consuming, inefficient, and often fails to capture and quantify students' learning progress and challenges comprehensively. With advancements in technology, especially in text recognition and machine learning, new avenues have opened up for automating this review process. This allows for a more efficient and systematic analysis of students' learning situations. This study aims to explore how these technologies can be utilized to automatically identify and analyze key information in students' handwritten notes. The goal is to assess students' learning outcomes and understanding more effectively. By automating the recognition and analysis of handwritten notes, the study seeks to provide educators with a powerful tool to monitor students' learning progress more accurately, identify learning obstacles, and offer personalized feedback and support based on individual needs. This paper introduces a technology integrating Attention Multi-task U-Net and GPT-4 for extracting data from handwritten notes. The method facilitates better understanding and analysis of student notes, offering teachers precise learning data and aiding students in receiving personalized learning support. The study underscores its potential in educational technology, particularly in improving teaching quality and student learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Landing location planning based on genetic cooperative particle swarm optimization
abstract: Being able to safely land on the surface is one of the primary challenges when a probe exploring an asteroid. In order to ensure landing safety, the landing location planning needs to comprehensively consider the terrain characteristics and avoid obstacles such as protruding rocks, craters and slopes. Relatively flat areas are suitable for landing. If multiple landers are landing together, in order to avoid collisions and maintain good communication, appropriate distance should be maintained between the landers. In this paper, we first establish a landing environment model, and then propose a landing location planning method for a lander-group using genetic cooperative particle swarm optimization (GCPSO), which ensures the autonomous movement of individual landers while maintaining a certain safe landing distance between them. Taking a group of three landers as an example, simulation experiments show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can ensure the group to achieve stable landing and keep safe distances between them.

articleTitle: Cooperative tracking control of cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems via adaptive neural backstepping
abstract: This paper aims to address cooperative tracking control problem of cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems via adaptive neural backstepping approach. Firstly, based on unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), the mathematical modeling of the cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems is carried out. Then, to construct the communication network of the cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems, the network topology theory is employed. Moreover, combined with distributed backstepping approach and radial basis function neural network, the adaptive controller is designed to realize the distributed cooperative tracking control of cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems. Furthermore, the three-dimensional motion environment modeling of the cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems is developed through MATLAB-NETLOGO co-simulation platform. Based on this, the visualization display of cooperative tracking control of cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems is achieved. Finally, by example analysis, the proposed distributed cooperative tracking algorithm for cross-domain heterogeneous unmanned systems is reliable and effective.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Tank Gun Pointing Control System based on Singular Perturbation Theory
abstract: To solve the problem of realizing high-precision pointing control in tank gun pointing control systems due to nonlinear factors such as dead zone, coupling, and joint flexibility, a robust control system based on singular perturbation theory was proposed. This control method does not need to prefabricate the gear gap size, and only needs the angular displacement of the turret and barrel, its angular velocity size feedback, without needing higher-order feedback. Firstly, the nonlinearity of the dead zone is dealt with by establishing a mathematical model of the coupling of the horizontal turret and the vertical barrel in the aiming control system of a tank gun. Second, the system is decoupled into two subsystems with different time scales of fast and slow by the singular perturbation theory. A robust control law based on the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaac inequality is designed for the slow subsystem, and a differential control law is designed for the fast subsystem to enhance its stability and anti-perturbation capability. Lyapunov’s theorem and Lasalle’s invariance theorem are used to prove the stability of the control system. In the end, the control scheme proposed in this paper is compared with the optimal control scheme of the nonlinear decoupling control system. The result shows that the control scheme proposed in this paper has a good anti-jamming ability and a good dynamic steady-state performance.

articleTitle: Predefined Performance Control for Saturation Nonlinear Systems in Finite-Time
abstract: This paper investigates predefined performance control (PPC) in finite-time for nonlinear systems under saturation nonlinearity and immeasurable states. A modified finite-time performance function is devised to obtain expected performance indexes within finite-time. Meanwhile, the impact of input saturation is overcome by using mean-value theorem. By integrating backstepping method with adaptive technique, an observer-based PPC algorithm is presented, which guarantees that tracking error converges into predefined range within finite-time. Finally, the validity of presented control algorithm is demonstrated via simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-Objectives Optimization with Digital Twin for Mixed-flow Production Line
abstract: The automatic mixed-flow production line plays a pivotal role in the manufacturing industry due to its highly flexible production capacity. Addressing challenges such as equipment configuration, multi-resource allocation, and capacity optimization in printed circuit board mixed-flow production lines, this paper proposes a dynamic optimization method based on digital twinning (DT). By constructing the twin body of the printed circuit board production system, a comprehensive mathematical optimization model leveraging digital twinning is introduced. The real-time operating data of the digital twin is used. Real-time operating data from the digital twin are utilized for resource allocation optimization, which is validated through experiments. This method has solved the problems of the low balance loss rate and bottleneck processes. This approach effectively resolves issues related to low balance loss rates and bottleneck processes, offering theoretical support for online resource optimization in production line systems.

articleTitle: Singularity-Avoidance Adaptive Predefined-Time Event-Triggered Resilient Control for a QUAV with Unknown Actuator Faults
abstract: In this study, an adaptive predefined-time event-triggered resilient control strategy is proposed for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle with input saturation and unknown actuator faults. At first, the "explosion of complexity" problem in the traditional backstepping design process is successfully overcome by using the dynamic surface control technique. Then, by introducing the hyperbolic tangent function and fractional calculus item, the singularity-avoidance adaptive predefined-time event-triggered resilient controller is designed to alleviate the communication bandwidth burden and enhance the degree of freedom in controller design. Stability results prove that the proposed control scheme ensures that all signals in the closed-loop system are predefined-time bounded. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Cost-Minimized Partial Computation Offloading in Heterogeneous Edge-Cloud Systems
abstract: Nowadays, Internet of Things Devices (IOTDs) support numerous applications that require extensive computational resources and are sensitive to delays. Nevertheless, IOTDs are constrained by limited computational power and battery life, preventing them from processing all tasks in real-time. Computation offloading provides a solution to these problems where IOTDs can offload part of their tasks to edge servers for execution. Small Base Stations (SBSs) are located closer to IOTDs, which act as edge servers. However, SBSs have limited computing resources compared with a Cloud Data Center (CDC). Therefore, a heterogeneous edge-cloud system is often deployed in urban areas for computation offloading. In addition, attaining the lowest cost in such a system while satisfying the delay requirements of tasks presents a significant challenge. In this work, a computation offloading strategy aimed at minimizing the overall system cost is proposed. Initially, an optimization problem with real-world constraints is defined, leveraging the hybrid architecture as its basis. Then, a novel swarm optimization algorithm named Grey wolf optimization embedded with Simulated annealing and Genetic learning (GSG) is proposed to solve this optimization problem. GSG optimizes resource allocation and task offloading among IOTDs, SBSs, and CDC. Simulation experiments involving real-life tasks demonstrate that GSG achieves a significantly lower system cost than its existing peers.

articleTitle: Performance-based Fault-tolerant Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems with Actuator Failures
abstract: In this paper, a performance-based fault-tolerant control method is proposed, whose purpose is to ensure stable operation even at the failure situation. A prescribed performance function-based supervision mechanism is proposed, which can detect the occurrence of an extreme failure. Also, a control strategy with low computational complexity is proposed, which can recover the system performance to its original level within a preset time after an extreme failure. Furthermore, its effectiveness is verified through the simulation.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Fusion Estimation for Power System Based on Channel Gain Encryption*
abstract: This paper studies distributed fusion estimation for power system, where smart sensors generate local estimates and send them to fusion center through wireless communication channels in presence of an eavesdropper. To protect power system state privacy, the privacy-preserving method based on artificial noise technique is introduced, which is designed by using channel gain encryption for each sensor. A sufficient condition on artificial noise is provided to make the eavesdropper’s expected error covariance unbounded for power system while the user’s fusion estimator will not deteriorate. Numerical example of single machine infinite bus power system is presented to verify our results.

articleTitle: Intermediate Variable Estimator-based Fault-tolerant Formation Control of Multi-agent Systems with Multiple Leaders
abstract: This paper addresses the distributed fault-tolerant formation control problem for a multi-leader systems subject to process faults. A fault estimation observer based on intermediate variables is utilized, in which the observer matching condition is not necessary. The fault estimation values obtained by the observer are applied to reconstruct the controller. By solving linear matrix inequalities and applying the Schur complement theorem, the observer gains are obtained. Subsequently, the controller gains are designed based on the properties of the Laplacian matrix and adaptive techniques. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Modeling and controller design of vertical take-off and landing turbojet powered aircraft
abstract: Aiming at the problems such as high altitude flight difficulty and poor wind resistance of rotary-wing UAV in disaster rescue, this paper proposes a vertical take-off and landing turbojet powered aircraft. The vehicle uses fuel as its power source, and four turbojet engines with vector propulsion systems provide thrust. Aiming at the difficult problem of controller design caused by complex nonlinear characteristics of aircraft, a T-S modeling method of aircraft is presented. Firstly, a dynamic model of the aircraft is established by analyzing the relationship between the force and rotation of the aircraft. On this basis, the T-S fuzzy model of aircraft is established by using sector nonlinear method. The model can decompose the complex nonlinear system into several simple linear subsystems, which is more convenient for controller design and analysis. To verify the validity of the T-S model, a fuzzy LQR controller is designed. Simulation results show that the designed controller can realize fast stabilization of the system. The structure design of the aircraft and T-S fuzzy control are of great practical significance for disaster relief in the complex plateau environment.

articleTitle: Distributed Fault-Tolerant Collision Avoidance Control of Multiple UAVs
abstract: In this paper, the distributed fault-tolerant tracking control and collision avoidance problem is investigated for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with actuator failures. First, a formation controller based on backstepping control is designed to track the target trajectory. Then, an adaptive parameter update law is developed to address the UAVs actuator failures and an improved artificial potential function is discussed for collision avoidance. Finally, simulation results of two UAVs are given to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Estimation State of Charge for Lithium Battery Based on Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper mainly studies the estimation problem of lithium battery SOC with time-varying noises in battery systems. First, a state space model of the lithium battery is established, and the model parameters of the battery system are obtained through parameter identification methods. Subsequently, an adaptive noises-resistant noises estimator for time-varying noises was designed, and an adaptive unscented Kalman filter (AUKF) with high filtering accuracy is proposed to obtain a more accurate SOC. Finally, the proposed algorithm is validated to be effective and highly accurate through lithium-ion battery experiment.

articleTitle: An Attention Learning Particle Swarm Optimizer with Sensitive Search Transition
abstract: Particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been extensively applied to diverse optimization problems, yet it may encounter challenges such as premature convergence and slow convergence, especially in complex optimization problems. Thus, how to guide particles away from local optima and exploit promising areas promptly becomes important for improving the performance of PSO. Considering the above issues, we propose an attention learning particle swarm optimizer with sensitive search transition (ALPSO-SST). In ALPSO-SST, the specially designed attentional learning (AL) strategy allocates higher attention to learning targets with superior quality, so that the learning targets are integrated into an attentional particle with these diverse attentions. Such an attentional particle guides the population toward superior areas. Additionally, through employing the principle of probability distribution entropy, the evolution level of the population can be sensitively captured by a specially designed evolution indicator, enabling a sensitive search transition (SST) from exploration to exploitation. Experimental results demonstrate that ALPSO-SST outperforms five PSO-based algorithms across eight well-known test functions in both convergence speed and solution quality, offering promising prospects for future research and applications in real-world optimization problems.

articleTitle: Lightweight Network for Real-Time Segmentation of Endoscopic Surgical Instruments
abstract: Real-time segmentation of surgical instruments is a fundamental technique in robot-assisted surgical navigation and plays a key role. Despite significant progress in natural image segmentation in recent years, practical realization of accurate real-time semantic segmentation of operative instruments in endoscopy is still a challenging topic. In this paper, we build a lightweight network that can meet real-time requirements while maintaining segmentation accuracy. Specifically, our model adopts an encoder-decoder structure, where the bottleneck for semantic feature extraction is constructed in the encoder part by combining the Ghost module and MobileNetV3, the decoder consists of a depth-separable convolution, an attention module, and a transposed convolution. The depth-separable convolution used reduces the parameters and computation of the model, the attention module captures the global context and encodes the semantics, emphasizes key semantic features and improves the representation of the features, and this module has only a few parameters, which helps to localize the surgical instruments. The model is validated on the EndoVis 2017 dataset to prove the proposed model, and the results show that the method can excellently accomplish the semantic segmentation of surgical instruments, and its inference speed meets the real-time requirement, which provides a reference for further robot-assisted surgical navigation.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Feature Fusion Network with Transformer for Change Detection of Remote Sensing Images
abstract: With the increasing attention of the state to land resources, change detection is an important task in land resource management, cropland and forest protection and road damage detection. Although image difference-based methods can effectively detect changes between before and after images, they are not ideal when facing significant pseudo-changes. However, considering that the vision transformer (ViT) is difficult to accomplish the pixel-level semantic segmentation task and the transformer-UNet structure is too complex, we propose a multi-scale feature fusion network (MSFF-net). It combines the feature information of two images and improves the accuracy of prediction results. The experimental results show that the change detection performance of MSFF-net is significantly better than several current classical methods.

articleTitle: The Utilization of Virtual Simulation Software and the Introduction of Fault Points in Microcontroller Education
abstract: In the realm of traditional microcontroller education, there exist certain deficiencies and challenges that hamper students' learning experiences, such as monotonous teaching methods, theoretical overload, and passive knowledge absorption. To address these issues, this paper proposes the application of Proteus simulation software in microcontroller education, accompanied by the introduction of fault points to cultivate students' thinking abilities, observational skills, troubleshooting proficiency, and hands-on capabilities within the instructional design.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Representation Learning on Event Stream
abstract: The spatiotemporal correlation of events obtained by event camera contains the operational laws of moving targets. For deeper understanding events, an effective spatiotemporal representation learning-based model is desired. Note that events are dense in time and sparse in space, how to capture the global correlations of all events in the event stream simultaneously while well addressing the sparse input is a challenging task. To fulfil this task, an Elastic Net-incorporated tensor network (ENTN) model is proposed in this work with twofold ideas: a) utilizing a fully-connected 3rd-order tensor network for tensor decomposition to implement spatiotemporal representation learning on event stream, b) incorporating Elastic-net regularization to perform better feature selection. Experimental results indicate that ENTN can represent the spatiotemporal correlation of events in an event stream with high quality.

articleTitle: Marine Navigation Radar Target Detection with Multi-scale Spatiotemporal Feature Fusion-based Deep Learning
abstract: This article endeavors to tackle the challenge of radar target detection in dynamic scenarios characterized by strong maneuvering, such as those involving rotating radar carriers or high-speed moving targets. A deep learning model, termed the multi-scale spatiotemporal fusion network (MSSF-Net), is proposed to effectively tackle the aforementioned scenarios. The proposed method encompasses several modules, with a notable inclusion being the improved Faster R-CNN module, which incorporates attention and spatial transformation mechanisms. This integration enables the extraction of spatial offset features from the current frame’s echo image, facilitating the suppression of sea clutter and noise. Concurrently, the spatiotemporal feature fusion module within the network is designed to extract spatiotemporal information from historical frame echo images. It conducts multi-scale and multi-level feature fusion with the feature maps generated by other modules. This enables the capture of profound spatiotemporal features from a global perspective, thereby mitigating the decline in detection accuracy induced by the spatial shift of echo information resulting from strong maneuvering. Other modules within the method serve to manage the input and output of the model. Simulation results validate the enhanced accuracy of radar target detection achieved by the method under conditions of strong maneuvering.

articleTitle: Backdoor Attack Based on Privacy Inference against Federated Learning
abstract: As a pioneering distributed learning framework, federated learning (FL) has gained widespread adoption. It operates collaboratively among participants, with communication limited to sharing model parameters between the server and participants. However, FL is also more susceptible to active attacks from malicious insiders. Poisoned updates submitted by attackers can degrade the performance of the global model. Previous research only considered using the naive data of malicious clients for backdoor poisoning, and therefore achieved limited backdoor attack success rates. In this paper, we propose a novel Federated Backdoor Attack based on Privacy Inference (FBA-PI). Combining privacy inference based on generative adversarial networks (GAN), the attacker first infers sensitive information from victim participants and then injects backdoor triggers into the naive and generated data. Finally, malicious clients can embed backdoor semantics into the global model by participating in regular federated aggregation. Extensive experiments on the MNIST dataset verify the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A High-speed and Lightweight Siamese Tracker based on RepVGG Network
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of neural networks, visual object tracking is becoming increasingly important in real-world applications such as camera drones and driving assistant systems, even self-driving technology. Neural network-based Siamese trackers achieve satisfactory accuracy in the object tracking field and stand out. However, high-performance Siamese trackers are often designed to be complex and heavy, which hinders their application on resource-limited mobile devices. Thus, compressing the neural network-based tracker to make it lightweight and efficient without obvious performance degradation is of great significance. Inspired by the outstanding work of RepVGG which focuses on compressing multi-branches neural networks without any accuracy cost, we propose the RepSiamses Tracker (RST) which is extremely lightweight and achieves very high tracking speed. In RST, the RepVGG-based backbone depth can be adapted to the different target hardware which benefits from the high flexibility of RepVGG. The experimental results on the high-quality benchmark VOT2018 and LaSOT show that RST achieves satisfactory accuracy and extremely high tracking speed on GPU. More impressively, RST is able to run on the CPU at a hyper-real-time of 69 fps and with very little memory cost of 16.4 MB. Such high tracking speed and low memory cost can bridge the gap between academic algorithms and real-world applications.

articleTitle: Tensor Graph Convolutional Network for Dynamic Graph Representation Learning
abstract: Dynamic graphs (DG) represent evolving interactions between entities in various real-world scenarios. Many existing DG representation learning models employ a combination of graph convolutional networks and sequence neural networks to capture spatial-temporal dependencies. However, this hybrid approach often fails to effectively capture the spatial-temporal continuity inherent in DGs. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called the Tensor Graph Convolutional Network (TGCN) to learn DG representations within a unified convolution framework based on tensor products. Our approach is founded on two key principles: (a) representing DG information in tensor form, and (b) leveraging tensor product operations to design a graph convolutional network that simultaneously models spatial and temporal features. Experimental results on three real-world DG datasets demonstrate that our proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Extended NNs-Based Adaptive Event-Triggered Asymptotic Control for Nonlinear Systems Against Actuator Faults
abstract: In this article, an adaptive event-triggered asymp¬totically fault-tolerant control (FTC) issue for nonlinear systems with actuator faults is investigated. An extended neural networks (NNs) technique is introduced to estimate unknown functions of the system under consideration. Compared with traditional NNs that ignore approximation errors, the proposed extended NNs further processes approximation errors, reducing the conservatism of the proposed algorithm. Then, within the framework of backstepping method, a new adaptive control strategy is developed by combining event-triggered mechanism (ETM) and bound estimation (BE) approach, which ensures the asymptotic convergence of system states while also reducing the transmission of unnecessary information, thus improving the utilization of communication resources. At the same time, the designed controller eliminates the adverse effects of actuator failures and system nonlinear terms. Finally, a simulation example of a single-link robot system is provided to demonstrate that the developed control strategy can ensure that all signals are bounded and system states are asymptotically convergent.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Input Constraint Control of a Vehicle-Manipulator System With Disturbance
abstract: The primary content of this article is the design and research of position tracking and vibration displacement control algorithm for a vehicle-manipulator system with asymmetric input constraint and uncertain disturbances. The dynamic of such a vehicle-manipulator system can be seen and described as the coupling of a number of integral-partial differential equations. For the considered asymmetric input constraint, two auxiliary systems are put forward as useful solution to handle asymmetric input saturation issue and a simple and efficient PD control algorithm is also proposed to guarantee the realization of position tracking and vibration displacement control. Finally, in addition to the Lyapunov’s theory, numerical simulation results also illustrate that the control effect of proposed algorithm is satisfactory.

articleTitle: A time-varying parameter identification algorithm based on prescribed-time convergence
abstract: This paper investigates parameter identification for time-varying parameter systems within prescribed time. In contrast to finite-time and fixed-time methods, the new algorithm guarantees convergence within a physically acceptable timeframe, regardless of the system’s initial state and parameters. The stability and boundedness of the time-varying parameter identification algorithm are demonstrated by using Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, numerical simulation examples of a Van der Pol oscillation circuit based on a memristor are presented to confirm the algorithm’s efficacy in practice.

articleTitle: Active vibration isolation method for cold atomic gravimeter based on high-gain observer sliding mode control
abstract: The article presents an advanced control strategy for cold atom gravimeter, leveraging high-gain observer sliding mode control. This approach involves several key steps: establishing a rigorous active vibration isolation model for cold atomic gravimeters; designing an optimized active vibration isolation system. The high-gain observer of this system effectively mitigates uncertainties associated with internal parameter variations and external ground vibrations. By incorporating fixed disturbances, the observer ensures accurate monitoring of these disturbances. Additionally, a sophisticated high-gain observer sliding mode control law is developed to address the limitations of traditional control methods, which often overlook the stochastic nature and model uncertainties of external disturbances like ground vibrations. This advanced control method rapidly converges the vibration velocity and displacement of the active vibration isolation system of cold atomic gravimeters, significantly enhancing the overall control accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Active Complementary Fault-tolerant Optimal Control for Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems based on ADP Technique
abstract: In this paper, a fully distributed active complementary fault-tolerant coordination control problem is addressed for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) under multiplicative actuator faults over undirected graph. To estimated the multiplicative actuator faults, an adaptive fault estimate scheme is constructed, based on which, a new system dynamics is built. Moreover, a cost function is introduced to obtain the active optimal complementary falut-tolerant control through adaptive dynamic programming (ADP). Finally, a simulation result is unfolded to demonstrate the effectiveness and performance of our scheme.

articleTitle: Complete Coverage Path Planning Based on BINND and MK-means++
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low information utilization efficiency and poor quality in the search field, a complete coverage path planning method is proposed, which introduces the concept of biological incentives to improve backtracking search and dynamically allocates areas using the modified K-means++ algorithm (MK-means++). A dynamic function is designed to carry the probability information in the environment, in order to solve the problems of low path planning efficiency and low environmental information utilization caused by the lack of probability prior knowledge. In order to improve the problems of high cost of escape paths and low value of temporary target points in traditional methods, the method Biologically Inspired Neural Network Decision (BINND), combining the idea of biological incentives with the backtracking search method, is designed. In order to solve the problem of unreachable areas due to the distribution of obstacle areas and starting points in the same allocation area, the area allocation mechanism, based on MK-means++ with obstacle information, is designed. The simulation results show that the path planning method has a better modeling effect and can improve the reachability of collaborative traversal process, which verifies the effectiveness, progressiveness, robustness and real time performance of the method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Nonlinear System With Time-Varying Parameters and Unknown Time-varying Control Coefficient
abstract: In this paper, a stability control issue for a class of single-input single-output(SISO) time-varying nonlinear systems with mismatched uncertainties and completely unknown time-varying input coefficient is investigated. Combining with the so-called congelation of variables method and a special type of Nussbaum function, a backstepping-based adaptive control scheme was proposed in our paper, which is able to achieve asymptotical stability in the presence of rapidly changing system parameters and absence of a priori knowledge of direction and amplitude of input coefficient. Through theory analysis and numerical simulation, it is demonstrated that the proposed algorithm guarantee the ultimately uniformly boundedness(UUB) of the signals in closed-loop system and realize asymptotical stability.

articleTitle: Prediction on the Accumulated Balance of Chinese Provincial Employee Medical Insurance Fund Based on GM (1,1) Model
abstract: The design of China's social medical insurance system is different from that of other countries. The existence of individual accounts of urban employee basic medical insurance has triggered a series of debates on the system rationality. Based on this, this study uses the grey prediction model to predict the accumulated balance of the employee medical insurance fund of each province from 2021 to 2030 by consulting the data of the statistical yearbook. The results show that the accuracy of using GM (1,1) model to predict the accumulated balance of employee medical insurance fund in each province is high, and the accumulated balance of employee medical insurance fund in each province will still increase significantly from 2021 to 2030. This result can be used as a reference for future changes in the accumulated balance of China's employee basic medical insurance fund, and provide data support for further policy improvement and reform.

Author Keywords: balance of employee medical insurance fund

articleTitle: Command filter-based fault-tolerant fast finite-time control of manipulator systems with sensor faults and event-triggered technology
abstract: For the trajectory tracking problem of a single-joint manipulator system with sensor faults. A fuzzy control system incorporating command filtering and event-triggered technology is devised to enhance system tracking accuracy. The problems of complicated calculation and influence of the filtering errors are solved by the introduction of the finite-time command filters and a compensation mechanism. During the controller design process, fuzzy logic systems are utilized to deal with the unknown functions in the systems. Hence, the suggested control scheme enhances the convenience and flexibility of controller design. Based on the numerical simulation analysis, it is shown that the better tracking performance can be achieved. In conclusion, it is concluded that our strategy is effective.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Multi-Agent Systems Based on Dynamic Event-triggered Mechanism: In Different Topologies
abstract: Under different communication topologies, this paper investigates the consensus problem for multi-agent systems with general linear dynamics under leader following. A distributed dynamic event-triggered control strategy with output feedback adjustment is proposed by using adaptive control technology of auxiliary variables, and it is applied to different follower communication topologies. The simulation results show that the leader-following systems under different communication modes of the followers can solve the completely distributed consensus problem. Moreover, the Zeno behavior of each multi-agent can be excluded. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by taking multi-vehicle cooperative tracking control as an example.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant Cooperative Control of Multiple Quadrotor UAVs Handling a Common Load
abstract: This paper focuses on the modeling and a generalized control framework for the coordinated quadrotor UAVs-Load transportation system. At first, the relatively complete dynamic models for multiple quadrotor UAVs are established under undetectable actuation faults and uncertain wind interference, considering the external effects of the load on the translational and rotational motions of each quadrotor UAV. And in order to transport the load smoothly and safely, the consensus control problem how to make the UAVs maintain the designed geometric configuration is formulated correspondingly. Finally, by introducing the virtual parameter estimation error into the Lyapunov function based on neighboring UAVs state information, the adaptive fault-tolerant controllers are developed to ensure that the defined synchronization errors for the UAVs position and attitude are uniform ultimate bound(UUB). The simulation results also prove the effectiveness of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: DevPF: Device identification through passive fingerprints in IoT
abstract: In the realm of Industrial IoT, devices are characterized by their diversity and complexity. Upon connection, these devices are exposed to a myriad of security threats. Nevertheless, the adoption of unique device fingerprints facilitates the secure identification and authentication of these devices during access. In this study, we propose DevPF, a novel framework for IoT device identification based on passive traffic analysis. Unlike traditional active detection methods, DevPF analyzes network traffic characteristics without interacting with devices, ensuring minimal network load and no interference with device operations. The framework utilizes machine learning algorithms to classify devices based on extracted traffic features. Experimental results on a public IoT dataset demonstrate that DevPF achieves high classification accuracy, making it a promising solution for enhancing the security of IoT networks.

articleTitle: Decomposition of multi-frequency signals in electric vehicles
abstract: The signal acquisition of electric vehicles is complex and variable. This study applied the traditional empirical mode decomposition (EMD) method to analysis the multi frequency signals of electric vehicle fault signals. It was found that, such signals mixed in colored noise is harmful for signal decomposition. In a classical bistable system, under the synergistic effect of adaptive stochastic resonance and EMD, the noise signal decomposition fails. Then, this article proposes a method that combines adaptive SR and EMD in periodic potential systems to achieve decomposition. At the same time, the Random Particle Swarm Optimization (RPSO) method was applied to determine optimal signal-to-noise ratio under condition of it reaches the peak value. According to the simulation results,it can be infered that this method is effective and valuable, and is benefit for signal processing in such field.

articleTitle: Data-Driven H ∞ Output Tracking Control of Linear Discrete-Time Systems
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of H <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> output tracking control for linear discrete-time systems with external disturbances. Two cases in which the disturbance is known and unknown are discussed. The matrix S-lemma is introduced to deal with the unknown disturbance. More importantly, Willems et al. Fundamental Lemma shows that the persistently exciting data can represent the input and output behavior of a linear system. By using the collected I/O data of the original system and reference system, a state feedback controller with a specified H <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance index is designed, which avoids the dependence on system dynamics knowledge and the potential modeling errors. Based on data-driven control (DDC) technology, the design of the controller is simplified and the designed controller ensures that the output of the closed-loop system tracks the output of the reference signal well. Finally, the simulation results of inverted pendulum system (IPS) verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Secure Remote State Estimation Against Eavesdropping Attacks Under Communication Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the problem of remote state estimation in the presence of malicious eavesdroppers and communication constraints. At any moment, the eavesdroppers can steal the communication data between the sensor and the remote state estimator. Besides, the communication constraints, including the utilization of Round-Robin protocols and the occurrence of packet dropout, are also taken into account. Based on the Paillier cryptosystem, a secure remote state estimator is designed to against eavesdropping attacks under the communication constraints. Then, under some mild assumptions, the unbiasedness and the consistency analyses are provided in detail. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed remote state estimator is corroborated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Sampling-Based Distributed Control for Quantized Consensus Tracking Under Denial-of-Service Attacks
abstract: In this paper, the quantized consensus tracking problem for continuous-time multi-agent systems (MASs) under denial-of-service (DoS) attacks is studied. Based on the dynamical quantized strategy, a sampling-based control protocol is developed, which is suitable for the high-order MASs under the general directed communication topology with limited bandwidth. To resist the DoS attacks, the scaling function is designed with a zooming-in and zooming-out approach. Sufficient conditions for consensus tracking problem under DoS attacks are provided, and the quantizer is unsaturated under the specified quantization level. Finally, simulation examples are provided to validate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Dynamic Programming-based Approximate Optimal Control for Collaborative Robot via Quintic Polynomial Planning
abstract: In this paper, we investigate adaptive dynamic programming-based quintic polynomial trajectory planning and optimal tracking control for collaborative robotic systems. According to polynomial interpolation, a quintuple polynomial trajectory planning method is proposed, which solves the problems of non-smooth angular velocity changes and jumps in acceleration with cubic polynomial interpolation. In addition, the optimal control strategy is solved by adaptive dynamic programming. Lyapunov functions are introduced to prove the stability of the control system. At last, the simulation results verify the truth of the above theory.

articleTitle: On the Edge Controllability of Multiple Dynamic Agents
abstract: This paper investigates the edge controllability of multi-agent networks with multiple dynamic agents that have both cooperative and antagonistic interactions. Using the transition relation between edge states and vertex states of the single-integrator network, the network model of multiple edge dynamics is established. Furthermore, under the leader-follower framework, the edge controllability for second-order-integrator, high-order-integrator and general linear dynamic networks are investigated based on consensus protocols. The results show that, under the leader’s position and topology are fixed, the edge controllability for multiple dynamic networks is equivalent to the corresponding single-integrator dynamic networks. In addition, the relations between vertex controllability and edge controllability are further discussed.

articleTitle: High Performance Control of Dynamical Formation by Estimation of Leader Information
abstract: To enhance the robustness and tracking performances of distributed systems with multiple agents in the presence of topological uncertainties and heterogeneous dynamics simultaneously, a distributed holographic state estimator of leader information is designed by sliding mode control theory and analyzed theoretically. The convergence performance of the designed information estimator does not depend on the dynamical model of agent, and only requires that the minimum eigenvalue of the topological matrix is greater than zero. With the estimated information of leader, a model predictive controller is designed for each one to ensure running safety and formation. In order to verify the adaptability of the designed system to uncertain communication topology and agent heterogeneity, both simulations and experiments have been carried out.

articleTitle: Time-varying Threshold Design for Intermittent Fault Detection of Dynamic Systems with Luenberger Observer☆
abstract: This paper is concerned with time-varying threshold design problem for timely and false-free Luenberger observer-based fault detection for dynamic systems subject to intermittent fault. A new time-varying threshold is proposed with considerations of external disturbance and system uncertainty, by considering threshold supremum, metastable threshold, decaying coefficient and time intervals repartition. Detailed analysis of convergence and detectability is given in the sense of Lyapunov theorem. A simulation example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of theoretical findings.

articleTitle: A novel decoupled knowledge distillation
abstract: Deep neural networks outperform their shallow counterparts, but they tend to add depth or width, leading to a surge in parameters and computations. It is well-established that excessively wide networks pose a heightened risk of overfitting, while overly deep networks demand a substantial computational burden. This paper introduces a novel narrow-deep ResNet architecture and applies the strategy of decoupled knowledge distillation. This innovation aims to enhance network depth while mitigating potential issues associated with excessive width. This involves establishing a trained teacher model to instruct the training of unaltered, wide, and narrow-deep ResNet(student) models, enabling students to learn from the teacher’s output. In order to assess the efficiency of this proposed method, We conduct tests on the Cifar-100 and Pascal VOC datasets. Results indicate that the method in this paper empowers a smaller model to achieve nearly identical accuracy as larger models, while significantly reducing inference time and computational effort.

articleTitle: Multiscale Complementary Semantic Enhancement Network for Welding Seam X-ray Image Defect Detection
abstract: The core challenge in the analysis of welding seam X-ray images is the problem of multiscale defects, where defects can range in size and shape from tiny pores to larger unpenetrated areas. However, the current methods have limitations, such as information loss during feature extraction and inadequate scale adjustment strategies during feature fusion, making it difficult for models to capture complex semantic information and retain key details effectively. In this paper, we propose a Multiscale Complementary Semantic Enhancement Network (MCSEN), which includes a Multi-level Semantic Enhancement (MSE) module and a Multi-level Feature Complementary Aggregation (MFCA) module. The MSE module improves multiscale feature learning through graph convolution-guided feature aggregation, effectively mitigating the problem of information loss and enhancing features’ distinguishability and semantic richness. The MFCA module resolves the issues of scale inconsistency and semantic discontinuity in feature fusion by adaptively generating fusion weights and finely adjusting feature allocation. Comprehensive experiments show that MCSEN achieves an overall average precision of 91.9%, significantly higher than other models.

articleTitle: Comparison of learning identification and recursive identification algorithms
abstract: This paper discusses learning least squares(LLS) identification algorithm and recursive least squares(RLS) algorithm for a kind of stochastic dynamic time-varying systems. Utilizing the corresponding learning algorithms and forgetting factor recursive least squares(FFRLS) algorithm conducts simulation, which indicates that learning algorithms are importance to parameter estimation.

articleTitle: Hindsight Experience Replay with Correlation Reward Mechanism
abstract: Robots have been increasingly applied in various fields with the development of technology and reinforcement learning interacts with the environment through policy models to achieve autonomous decision-making and effectively solve intelligent control problems for robots. However, robots still face significant challenges in completing tasks with sparse reward environments due to the difficulty in obtaining successful experiences after adopting reinforcement learning. Hindsight experience replay (HER) has been proven to be an effective method for dealing with sparse reward problems by setting virtual goals and learning equally from failed experiences. However, not all failed experiences have the same effect on the learning of real goals, and some virtual goals with low correlation with real goals may have a negative impact on the learning of real goals. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a reward mechanism named Correlation Based Hindsight Experience Replay (CBHER), which evaluates the correlation between the virtual target and the real target by calculating the angle and distance between them, and constructs a new reward mechanism based on correlation. This method ensures that virtual targets with higher correlation with the real target will receive higher reward values, thereby reducing the impact of virtual targets with lower correlation on the learning of the real target. Our method was validated in three simulated robot tasks to improve learning performance, and experimental results showed that our method is significantly superior to existing methods, with a training efficiency improvement of 17% compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: AUV Optical Vision Submarine Pipeline Inspection
abstract: In order to meet the practical needs of regular inspection of submarine pipelines, an optical vision inspection method for submarine pipelines mounted on Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is proposed. Methods by improving the dark channel algorithm, an adaptive red channel coefficient method was proposed to obtain the submarine pipeline image with higher quality and less noise. The improved Hough transform line feature extraction method is proposed as the strategy of submarine pipeline, so as to reduce the false detection rate and improve the calculation efficiency. The KCF filter is introduced to track the submarine pipeline. The accuracy and accuracy of the proposed algorithm are 94% and meet the requirements of real-time pipeline detection.

articleTitle: Robust performance control with prescribed time feature for strict-feedback systems under time-varying control gain
abstract: We propose a robust prescribed performance control strategy for nonlinear strict-feedback system under time-varying control coefficient in this paper, and the tracking error will converge to the preset error band in prescribed time. Our work addressed three issues. Firstly, we introduce unified performance function, normalized function and barrier function to convert the actual tracking error into analytical form, which can deal with global and semi-global conditions; Meanwhile, we propose the concept of transformed rate function. Together with the unified performance function, we achieve the prescribed-time feature. Finally, we use a special form of Nussbaum function to deal with the problem of time-varying control coefficients. The effectiveness of this strategy is verified by theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Dynamic State Estimation of Distribution Network Based on Strong Tracking Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter
abstract: Effective state estimation is a prerequisite for ensuring the safe, stable, and economical operation of distribution networks. The traditional cubic Kalman filter (CKF) typically assumes that the variance of system noise is constant and known.
