Then, the Pulp solution library was used to solve the possible ship one-on-one duel situation in the scenario, and two specific configuration plans for the problem were given using the idea of uncertain optimization. The results show that the model we proposed can solve the problem of ship resource configuration in naval wargame. This model can be widely applied to limited resource configuration problems in this type of imperfect information game.

articleTitle: WRES: A Low-Temperature Regulation and Enhancement System for Power Distribution Grid Maintenance Robots
abstract: Distribution grids extend the power grid towards each end users, therefore covering a wide range of latitudinal and climatic variations across the globe. Maintaining and servicing the distribution grids by human workers present significant life risks directly resulting from cold weather, making robotic replacement a pressing necessity. However, when facing similar cold-weather challenges, robots also require specific enhancements when the working climate conditions extend beyond their regular range of tolerance. With very few existing works tacking this issue, this work presents a lowtemperature enhancement and regulation system specifically for distribution grid maintenance robots. The main goal is to provide viable enhancements to continuously operate down to 30 degrees Celsius (-22 Fahrenheit) extreme ambient temperature, while optimizing battery life for longer operation time. The proposed system consists of a novel integrated temperature regulation system paired with an embedded element insulation layer for heat-dissipation control. A prototype system has been developed and tested in a series of validation experiments, demonstrating the efficacy and performances of the proposed system, paving the way to allweather robotic distribution grid maintenance under extreme cold conditions.

articleTitle: An ADRC-Incorporated Stochastic Gradient Descent Algorithm for Latent Factor Analysis
abstract: High-dimensional and incomplete (HDI) matrix contains many complex interactions between numerous nodes. A stochastic gradient descent (SGD)-based latent factor analysis (LFA) model is remarkably effective in extracting valuable information from an HDI matrix. However, such a model commonly encounters the problem of slow convergence because a standard SGD algorithm only considers the current learning error to compute the stochastic gradient without considering the historical and future state of the learning error. To address this critical issue, this paper innovatively proposes an ADRC-incorporated SGD (ADS) algorithm by refining the instance learning error by considering the historical and future state by following the principle of an ADRC controller. With it, an ADS-based LFA model is further achieved for fast and accurate latent factor analysis on an HDI matrix. Empirical studies on two HDI datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art LFA models in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy for predicting the missing data of an HDI matrix.

articleTitle: Neuroadaptive Fault-Tolerant Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems with New Time-Varying Constraints on States
abstract: In this article, a neuroadaptive fault-tolerant control scheme is proposed for a class of nonlinear systems with actuator failures, full state constraints and unknown time-varying disturbances. Besides the constraint boundary is different from the common research which is connected with time, partial states and desired trajectory. Additionally, we employ neural networks to approximate the unknown nonlinear functions, and the problem of "explosion of complexity" is avoided by utilizing the dynamic surface control technique during the design process of conventional backstepping control. The control scheme can guarantee the ultimate bounded stable tracking and the full state constraints are not violated. Both the theoretical analysis and numerical simulation are presented to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Autonomous Wave Tracking and Water Landing Control of Water UAV Based on Adaptive Dynamic Inverse
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dynamic glide trajectory for the autonomous landing of a fixed-wing water UAV in the presence of water surface waves. Additionally, control modes for pitch angle rate and speed in longitudinal motion are proposed using the adaptive dynamic inverse method. The longitudinal motion controller for the water UAV employs adaptive dynamic inverse control. Specifically, the pitch angle rate is considered as the innermost loop, the dynamic inverse control of the pitch angle loop is applied as the middle loop, and the pitch angle feedback serves as the outer loop. The MRAC (Model Reference Adaptive Control) method based on dynamic inverse is utilized to design the control law for the pitch angle rate and speed control loop. Nonlinear simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control law. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed longitudinal channel controller can accurately track the desired dynamic water landing trajectory, ensuring that the water UAV meets the safety requirements for water landing. The findings of this study hold significant engineering application value.

articleTitle: Perturbation analysis for reachability and controllability of probabilistic Boolean control networks based on the semi-tensor product
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of function perturbation on the reachability and controllability of probabilistic Boolean control networks (PBCNs) using the algebraic framework based on the semi-tensor product (STP) of matrices. The influence of perturbation on the reachability and controllability of PBCNs is classified into four cases according to whether the perturbed control can substitute the original one. For each case, a reachability perturbation matrix is constructed to demonstrate the changes in the reachability matrix caused by function perturbation. Based on this, some results of the perturbation analysis on the reachability and controllability of PBCNs are presented.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Exemplars Selection-based Differential Evolution Algorithm for Constrained Multi-objective Optimization
abstract: Constrained multi-objective optimization problems (CMOPs) pose a significant challenge due to the presence of multiple conflicting objective functions requiring optimization, alongside numerous complex constraints that must be satisfied. When employing evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to address such problems, it is imperative to simultaneously consider the diversity, convergence, and feasibility of the population. To address this concern, this paper introduces a differential evolution algorithm based on dynamic learning exemplars, named DESDE, wherein the selection of learning exemplars for each individual is determined through evolutionary algebra. Specifically, to generate offspring with diversity, individuals have a plethora of learning exemplars to choose from during the early stage of evolution, thus more promising regions can be explored. Moreover, to expedite population convergence in the later stage, only individuals with superior performance are chosen as learning exemplars. The experimental results, obtained from evaluating the algorithm on 29 test problems alongside five classic constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (CMOEAs), demonstrate the high competitiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fusing LiDAR and Radar with Pillars Attention for 3D Object Detection
abstract: In recent years, LiDAR has emerged as one of the primary sensors for mobile robots, enabling accurate detection of 3D objects. On the other hand, 4D millimeter-wave Radar presents several advantages which can be a complementary for LiDAR, including an extended detection range, enhanced sensitivity to moving objects, and the ability to operate seamlessly in various weather conditions, making it a highly promising technology. To leverage the strengths of both sensors, this paper proposes a novel fusion method that combines LiDAR and 4D millimeter-wave Radar for 3D object detection. The proposed approach begins with an efficient multi-modal feature extraction technique utilizing a pillar representation. This method captures comprehensive information from both LiDAR and millimeter-wave Radar data, facilitating a holistic understanding of the environment. Furthermore, a Pillar Attention Fusion (PAF) module is employed to merge the extracted features, enabling seamless integration and fusion of information from both sensors. This fusion process results in lightweight detection headers capable of accurately predicting object boxes. To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, extensive experiments were conducted on the VoD dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our fusion method, showcasing improved performance in terms of detection accuracy and robustness across different environmental conditions. The fusion of LiDAR and 4D millimeter-wave Radar holds significant potential for enhancing the capabilities of mobile robots in real-world scenarios. The proposed method, with its efficient multi-modal feature extraction and attention-based fusion, provides a reliable and effective solution for 3D object detection.

articleTitle: A Federal Recursive RUL Prediction Approach for Inter-Client Information Complementarity for Missing Data
abstract: RUL (Remaining useful life, RUL) prediction is one of the most important methods to ensure the safe operation of mechanical equipment. When continuous time segments are missing from the monitoring data, the relevant information from the sequence itself is not enough for a single RUL client to learn an accurate bearing degradation trend model. Therefore, a federated recursive RUL prediction method for inter-client information complementarity (FedRC) for missing data is proposed. High RUL prediction accuracy is ensured by information complementation within inter-client segments and gradual recursion between intra-client segments. A joint central loss function-driven aggregation weight and local loss joint optimization strategy is designed to reasonably allocate the weights of the uploaded model parameters of each client, which further improves the RUL prediction accuracy. In the case of missing local continuous time data segments, the proposed method ensures the RUL prediction accuracy through a segment-by-segment complementary recursive joint strategy among clients.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Analysis for robotic arm-hand systems
abstract: It is crucial for the motion planning, structure analysis and control design to construct the dynamic model (DM) for robot system. In this paper, we propose a mathematical modeling method for multi-finger arm robot, which represents a challenging issue due to the complexity and strong coupling of robotic arm-hand systems. Drawing inspiration from the genuine motion characteristics of the human arm and hand, we conceptualize the multi-finger system as a collection of robotic rigid manipulators. Guided by this concept, we introduce a uniform, low complexity modeling approach by using the Lagrange formulation and Denavit-Hartenberg convention, which is capable of constructing the dynamics for robotic arm-hand systems with arbitrary degree of freedom (DOF) in an analytical manner. Simple but effective, the resulting DM formulation is concise, further facilitating control design. Furthermore, a simulation upon using baseline PID control method is conducted to validate the proposed DM frame.

articleTitle: Task Allocation of Multiple AUVs and Simulation in Large Range Underwater Environment
abstract: This paper studies the task allocation problem of underwater multi-AUV system. The mathematical model for task allocation is established based on the characteristics of underwater multi-AUV system executing tasks. On this basis, we propose a task allocation method for multi-AUV system based on Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) neural network. The task allocation scheme is obtained by considering the competitive nature of SOM and addressing issues such as multiple task types, underwater currents, and moving task points that exist in the actual working environment of underwater multi-AUV system. The fitness function of the SOM task allocation algorithm is improved and validated through simulation comparisons. And the proposed algorithms in this paper are extended to larger underwater environment. Complex simulations involving multiple task types and large task volumes are conducted in large-scale underwater environment to validate the performance of the improved algorithm.

articleTitle: Attitude Consensus Tracking Control for Networked Uncertain Rigid Spacecraft with Prescribed Performance
abstract: In this study, we tackle the challenge of achieving attitude consensus tracking control for multi-spacecraft system, each spacecraft to uncertainties and operating under a directed network topology. This approach distinguishes itself from conventional methods by eliminating the need for specific initial conditions, thereby ensuring global tracking outcomes that are independent of such conditions. Additionally, we ensure that output consensus tracking is realized asymptotically, while adhering to any predetermined transient performance criteria within a finite time frame. The advancements presented herein are made possible through the utilization of a performance function coupled with prescribed-time observer.

articleTitle: Partial Discharge Pattern Recognition via Improved Evolutionary Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Deep learning has surfaced in numerous practical domains, including face recognition, autonomous driving, and fault detection. In recent times, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), emblematic of deep learning methodologies, have been employed extensively for pattern recognition tasks. Nonetheless, the current architecture of CNNs for pattern recognition heavily relies on domain expertise and entails extensive trial and error. To address this challenge, an evolutionary framework for CNNs has been devised to autonomously determine network architectures tailored for partial discharge pattern recognition. First, we transform the partial discharge data into images to eliminate the effect of noise in the data and perform feature extraction on the partial data. Subsequently, we outline a search space grounded on fundamental network components. Finally, we introduce a flexible variable-length encoding scheme along with corresponding reproduction operators. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, and we demonstrate higher recognition accuracy in two different real-world scenarios compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: DeepSwarm: A Deep Model for Swarm Motion Prediction Using Swin Transformer U-Net
abstract: Swarm behavior is characterized by coordinated movement among agents and has vital applications in various domains. Predicting swarm motion is critical for understanding the underlying mechanisms and dynamics of swarm behaviors. This paper focuses on the problem of swarm motion prediction and establishes a simulation dataset based on the Boids mathematical model. The conventional motion prediction problem is converted into a density map prediction task. A deep learning model, named DeepSwarm, is proposed to tackle this challenge. DeepSwarm leverages the 3D Swin Transformer U-Net architecture to capture spatio-temporal correlations at different granularities. To address the sparsity issue of the swarm density data, the Sparsity Enhanced Module (SEM) is introduced by generating foreground masks. The model is optimized using a combination of multiple loss functions which considers masks and values simultaneously. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed DeepSwarm in predicting swarm density maps. Further ablation studies demonstrate the significance of model components.

articleTitle: Spacecraft Attitude Fault-tolerant Maneuver Control with Flexible Prescribed Performance
abstract: This paper studies fault-tolerant control of the spacecraft attitude control system with prescribed performance under the coexistence of actuator faults, disturbances and uncertainties. First, a flexible appointed-time prescribed performance function (FAPPF) is proposed, which can significantly improve prescribed performance control robustness to unknown initial errors and avoid repeated and cumbersome parameter adjustments. Secondly, an equivalent fusion error is designed based on FAPPF, and terminal sliding mode is introduced to design a fault-tolerant controller, so that the attitude and angular rate meet the prescribed performance constraints at the same time. Further, the improved gray wolf optimization algorithm (IGWO) is introduced for online tolerant allocation of actuator control, which satisfies saturation and fault constraints while reducing energy consumption. Finally, numerical simulation proves the controller’s superiority and robustness.

articleTitle: Designing an Intelligent Medication Cabinet Based on STM32
abstract: General Secretary Xi Jinping, in his report at the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, advocated for advancing the construction of a Healthy China. This entails the development and strengthening of the healthcare workforce, with a particular focus on rural areas and communities. Furthermore, emphasis will be placed on enhancing the infrastructure for public health and environmental well-being. Promoting a civilized and healthy lifestyle will be encouraged, alongside intensified efforts in health promotion and education. The main focus of this study encompasses several aspects. Firstly, the development of a hardware master control program that enables the collection of temperature and humidity data. This data is then utilized to compare against predefined thresholds, facilitating the control of the cooling module and ventilation system to achieve the desired temperature. Secondly, the integration of the K210 visual module as a foundation for facial recognition, thereby enabling a unlocking function. Lastly, the utilization of the JDY-31 Bluetooth module to transmit data to a terminal, addressing challenges such as difficulties in obtaining medication in communities and hospitals, and alleviating the scarcity of essential medicines in rural areas.

articleTitle: Optimal Guaranteed Cost Hierarchical Sliding Mode Control for Under-Actuated Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This paper devotes to solving the adaptive optimal guaranteed cost control problem for switched under-actuated nonlinear systems (SUANS) in nominal form. An actor-critic (AC) network architecture with hierarchical sliding-mode surface (HSMS) is first established. As the system moves on the HSMS, the original system stability issue turns into the issue of designing approximate optimal control policies. Subsequently, a HSMS-based Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation is constructed by utilizing Bellman's principle of optimality, and the approximate solution of the HSMS-based HJB equation is gained via employing AC neural networks (NNs). It is noted that the AC updating laws of this paper are synchronously tuned, which achieves the simplification of the ADP process. Afterwards, a HSMS-based approximate optimal guaranteed cost control scheme is developed under AC dual NNs architecture. Finally, the practicality of the developed adaptive optimal guaranteed cost control scheme is verified by using a practical ball-arc system.

articleTitle: Capacity Degradation Estimation of Lithium Battery Based on Intelligent Particle Filter
abstract: With the booming development of the UAV industry, lithium-ion batteries are gradually being commonly used. For lithium-ion batteries, accurately estimating their battery life degradation can calculate the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries. Thereby, improving the reliability of lithium-ion battery-driven products and effectively reducing internal and external failure risks. As the current electric charge status of lithium-ion batteries cannot be directly obtained, their capacity degradation model has strong nonlinearity and non-Gaussian characteristics. In order to enhance the accuracy of capacity degradation estimation for lithium-ion batteries, this paper analyses and models the capacity degradation process of lithium-ion batteries using an improved intelligent MH particle filtering algorithm, and compares the estimation results of the proposed new method (MHPF) with those of classical PF and AGPF. The results prove that MHPF can obtain more reliable capacity degradation estimation results for lithium-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Temporal Logic Guided Affordance Learning for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
abstract: Reinforcement learning has shown great potential to address long-horizon tasks. However, most existing work lacks the ability to reason about functional parts of objects and extract the task semantics to facilitate robotic learning, making it difficult to achieve category-level generalization even on seen objects. To address these issues, we develop a temporal logic guided affordance learning framework for generalizable dexterous manipulations (TALD). In particular, TALD is equipped with affordance learning for predicting actionable information and LTL representation for understanding the task semantics and improving learning efficiency. We design a contact predictor from the affordance learning perspective to improve the generalization performance, which predicts the max-affordance point observation based on the 3D point clouds to guide the agent to manipulate the functional part of objects. And we exploit the LTL progression to construct a task-driven labeled POMDP to address the challenge of a non-Markovian reward function, and design a task module to extract the LTL representation by Transformer Encoder to improve the sampling efficiency and facilitate the robotic learning. We validate the proposed method in four articulated manipulation scenarios. The generalization performance corresponding to success rates and visualization effects show the effectiveness of TALD. Our project is available at: https://sites.google.com/view/tald-0257/.

articleTitle: A Life Cycle Management Architecture for Power Equipment Based on Device Fingerprinting
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving technological landscape, ensuring the efficiency, security, and longevity of power hardware and software equipment is paramount. This paper proposes a comprehensive life cycle management method that leverages device fingerprinting technology to optimize the management of such equipment throughout its entire life cycle. By uniquely identifying each device based on its distinct characteristics, the method establishes a robust security framework that enhances protection against unauthorized access and potential cyber threats. Moreover, the method facilitates efficient monitoring, analysis, and optimization of power equipment performance, leading to improved reliability and reduced downtime. Additionally, the integration of digital twin further enhances the management process by providing real-time insights and predictive analytics, enabling proactive maintenance and decision-making. Through a detailed exploration of the method’s components and implementation strategies, this paper offers insights into how organizations can effectively manage their power infrastructure while simultaneously enhancing security, operational efficiency, and leveraging the capabilities of digital twin.

articleTitle: Exploring the Relation between Geometric and Semantic Information for Semantic Segmentation of 3D Point Cloud
abstract: The emergence of 3D point cloud data has significantly advanced computer vision. Semantic segmentation of 3D real scene point clouds stands out as one of the most formidable challenges in this domain. Despite progress, many existing methodologies suffer from issues such as information loss, redundancy in local contexts, and inadequacies in decoding layer fitting. To tackle these obstacles, a receptive field reconstruction (RFR) mechanism is introduced to address information loss and diminish redundancy in local contexts. Secondly, we present a novel bilateral augmentation module, named the bilateral cross-augment (BCA) module, to bolster the relationship between geometric features and contextual data. Thirdly, an attention-based feature propagation (AFP) module is introduced for upsampling, enabling the adaptive restoration of local features from global context. Additionally, a 3D semantic segmentation network is crafted based on the U-Net architecture. Experimental evaluations are conducted on both the S3DIS large-scale real scene indoor dataset and the SemanticKITTI outdoor benchmarks, yielding state-of-the-art mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) scores compared to recent point-based MLP methods. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation experiments are carried out to showcase the superiority of the proposed modules

articleTitle: Data-Driven Geometric Control Method to the Attitude Control of a Carrier Rocket
abstract: The focus of this paper is to obtain a data-driven model of the rocket using a manifold-based approach and designing the controller for closed-loop rocket dynamics system. To meet the requirements of the optimal model, appropriate orthogonal decomposition is utilized to select low-order subspaces, and the state space model is fitted to the subspaces using the least squares method. On this basis, iterative algebraic equations for the construction of optimal feedback under Hamiltonian cohomology conditions are derived by designing gradient-based minimisation algorithms in convex positive definite matrix manifold functions. Finally, we demonstrate the reliability of the proposed manifold optimisation algorithm for a rocket attitude control model.

articleTitle: Neuroadaptive Tracking Control for Uncertain Stochastic Pure Feedback Systems with Prescribed Performance
abstract: In this paper, our focus is on prescribed performance control (PPC), a method that specifically targets a class of uncertain stochastic nonlinear systems exhibiting a pure feedback form. Firstly, we employ the mean value theorem to decouple the pure feedback form inherent in the system. In addition, the neural network and dynamic surfance techniques are exploited to identify the unknown dynamics. And utilizing the backstepping technique, a novel neuroadaptive control algorithm is developed to achieve the desired performance while tracking the reference signal. The proposed adaptive PPC scheme guarantees that all closed-loop signals maintain uniform ultimate boundedness in probability. Furthermore, the proposed scheme ensures tight tracking of the reference signal, thus attaining prescribed performance control. Lastly, simulation results are presented to demonstrate the practical feasibility of our approach.

articleTitle: A Multi-grained Cascade Structure for Online Sparse Streaming Feature Selection
abstract: Online Streaming Feature Selection (OSFS) is an efficient way to handle high-dimensional streaming data. While in real applications, streaming data often have a large amount of missing data due to various reasons, leading to the accuracy loss of OSFS. Latent Factor Analysis (LFA) is one of the most effective methods to pre-estimate the missing data of sparse streaming data. However, the known data density of sparse streaming features is always low, which is not enough for LFA to achieve the satisfactory pre-estimating performance for OSFS. Motivated by this, this paper proposes a sparse OSFS algorithm based on a multi-grained cascaded structure, termed as SO-MCS. Its main idea is two-fold: 1) using LFA to pre-estimate the missing data in sparse flow features in advance, and 2) gradually generating synthetic data to construct a multi-layer LFA architecture, which develops the known data density of the input sparse streaming feature matrix. Extensive experiments are carried out on eight real-world datasets, demonstrating that SO-MCS outperforms five state-of-the-art OSFS algorithms to a significant extent.

articleTitle: Prescribed Performance Control for Pure-Feedback Systems with Unknown Control Coefficients
abstract: This paper investigates the performance control problem of pure-feedback systems with unknown coefficients. To tackle the substantial control issue in nonlinear systems with unknown control coefficients, we employ a specialized Nussbaum function. In addition, we have proposed a prescribed performance control approach grounded in robust techniques, Its objective is to guarantee the convergence of the output error to an arbitrarily small residual set within a predefined threshold. The results demonstrate that under the influence of the proposed control rate, the boundedness of all signals within the closed-loop system is ensured. Moreover, the prescribed steady-state and transient tracking performance is attained.

articleTitle: Investigation of an sEMG Signal-Based Method for Online Hand Movement Classification
abstract: The human hand possesses remarkable dexterity and performs intricate tasks. Developing a reliable myoelectric prosthetic system for amputees is crucial. Although surface electromyographic (sEMG) signals have been utilized, their vulnerability to interference presents hurdles in hand movement identification. This work proposes a machine learning-based system for accurate recognition of hand movements. During the offline training process, artificial neural networks (ANN) have demonstrated superior performance compared to support vector machines and k-nearest neighbors, achieving a recognition rate of 99.63%. It underscores the exceptional ability of ANNs to learn complex nonlinear relationships within sEMG signals. Online experiments with a majority voting approach validated the feasibility of the system, reaching an average accuracy of 93.33%. This work provides technical support for fine control in myoelectric prosthesis, promising an improved quality of life for amputees.

articleTitle: Holographic Feedback Controlled Micro-Stereolithography for Constructing Microstructures with Tuned Mechanical Property
abstract: The fabrication of biocompatible scaffolds mimicking the stiffness of real human tissues holds paramount significance in the fields of tissue engineering and cell biology. However, existing stereolithography technologies still face challenges in precise control of the mechanical stiffness distribution of biological microstructures due to the difficulty in real-time monitoring of their mechanical properties during printing. In this study, we propose an innovative projection-based micro-stereolithography control method based on real-time holographic phase feedback to achieve high-precision fabrication of microstructures with region-specific mechanical stiffness distributions. Employing the minimum mean square error method, we calculate the optimal single mapping transformation matrix from holograph to DMD (digital micromirror device) mask for the corresponding calibration. The real-time holographic phase serves as feedback data to correct and modify the dynamic DMD mask. Additionally, adjusting the sampling interval and threshold parameters in feedback control enhances precision. Through this method, we constructed a complex mechanical property distribution of a windmill-shaped hydrogel microstructure. Experimental results demonstrate that our control method reduces the error in mechanical stiffness from 19.2 kPa in the case of no feedback control to 3.68 kPa, representing an 80.8% improvement in accuracy. The novel approach for constructing complex mechanical property distributions of microstructures in vitro has significant potential in tissue engineering in the future.

articleTitle: Beyond Traditional Driving Scenes: A Robotic-Centric Paradigm for 2D+3D Human Tracking Using Siamese Transformer Network
abstract: 3D human tracking plays a crucial role in the automation intelligence system. Current approaches focus on achieving higher performance on traditional driving datasets like KITTI, which overlook the jitteriness of the platform and the complexity of the environments. Once the scenarios are migrated to jolting robot platforms, they all degenerate severely with only a 20-60% success rate, which greatly restricts the high-level application of autonomous systems. In this work, beyond traditional flat scenes, we introduce Multi-modal Human Tracking Paradigm (MHTrack), a unified multimodal transformer-based model that can effectively track the target person frame-by-frame in point and video sequences. Specifically, we design a speed-inertia module-assisted stabilization mechanism along with an alternate training strategy to better migrate the tracking algorithm to the robot platform. To capture more target-aware information, we combine the geometric and appearance features of point clouds and video frames together based on a hierarchical Siamese Transformer Network. Additionally, considering the prior characteristics of the human category, we design a lateral cross-attention pyramid head for deeper feature aggregation and final 3D BBox generation. Extensive experiments confirm that MHTrack significantly outperforms the previous state-of-the-arts on both open-source datasets and large-scale robotic datasets. Further analysis verifies each component’s effectiveness and shows the robotic-centric paradigm’s promising potential when deployed into dynamic robotic systems.

articleTitle: Neural Operators for Robust State feedback Regulation of Hyperbolic PDEs
abstract: The recently introduced neural operator (NO) has been employed as a gain approximator in the backstepping stabilization control of hyperbolic and parabolic PDE systems. Due to the global approximation ability of the DeepONet, the NO generates the approximate spatial gain function with arbitrary accuracy. The closed-loop system stability can be ensured by the backstepping controller involving the approximate gain with sufficiently small error. In this paper, we extend the NO theory to a more complex field of robust regulation control for a class of hyperbolic PDE systems. The NO is trained offline on a dataset containing a sufficient number of prior solutions of the kernel equation, so as to generate feedback gain for the robust regulator. Based on the internal model principle, the regulator is inherently robust to the parameter uncertainty and the error in approximate gain. Therefore, the tracking error can still converge to 0 if the extended regulator equation is solvable. We provide a series of theory proofs of the regulation problem and a numerical test under the approximate gain. It is shown that NO is almost three orders of magnitude faster than PDE solver in generating kernel function, and the loss remains on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>. This provides an opportunity to use the NO methodology for accelerated gain scheduling regulation for PDEs with time-varying parameters.

articleTitle: Implementation of DWA Optimization Algorithm in Automatic Inspection of Switching Robot
abstract: In the secondary use of coal, the turbine generator converts thermal energy into electrical energy in the coal combustion process, which is supplied and distributed by the inverter, and the switching operations is carried out through the distribution room, which in turn realizes the control of circulating fluidized bed boiler. However, when the boiler fails, personnel arrival is not timely, chemical gas leakage and other problems will lead to technical failure. To improve the utilization and safety, this paper on the independent research and development of the switching robot hardware platform, to complete the distribution room multi-unit inspection, autonomous navigation tasks under the dynamic map, path planning algorithms are proposed. In the established map environment obtain the elementary information within the scene, establish the anchor point and ID information of the inspection point, and use the anchor point and ID information to carry out position correction to ensure that it accurately reaches the target position. A real-time dynamic map is used in the path planning process to update the original dynamic map so that the anchor point tracking and ID information can be obtained more accurately, and the reliability in long-term inspection in a similar environment is improved. The robot can obtain a very smooth trajectory with smoother motion under the actual working environment. The method proposed in this paper provides a feasible solution for the growing demand of automated inspection.

articleTitle: Research on Small Object Detection in Complex Marine Environments
abstract: With the improvement of computer arithmetic power, deep learning is evolving rapidly. Utilizing deep learning-based algorithms to the detection of floating objects at marine and marine rescue can not only save human and material resources but also improve efficiency. However, given the complex marine environments, it is hard for existing algorithms to achieve satisfactory results. In this paper, the SRB-YOLO detection method is proposed to add an image preprocessing module during the training process and input the images before and after preprocessing into the backbone network for training, to enhance the stability of the model, and improve the feature fusion network of the basic YOLOv5, which improves the detection result and increases the accuracy by seven percentage points.

articleTitle: Feature Transformation Based on Autoencoder to Oversample on Imbalanced Data
abstract: Imbalanced learning has gained many attentions in the domain of data mining and machine learning. Traditional classifiers often suffer from the under-representation of minority data with insufficient quantity in the training process. The remarkable data reconstruction abilities exhibited by autoencoders (AE) present us with a novel approach to oversample, named AE-OM. In this approach, AE is firstly hired to learn a manifold mapping that compresses critical features of majority samples nonlinearly. Then the manifold mapping is operated on minority samples to reconstruct new minority samples, where minority samples travel the same information route. The reconstructed minority samples not only capture the distribution information of raw positive samples but also filter noise. Conditional classifiers trained on datasets balanced with proposed method, AE-OM shows superior performance in terms of metrics of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,</inf> and AUC compared with 15 popular imbalanced methods.
